clue.text: See 17
Eat for a laugh, as they say

indicators.note: what people say is spoken, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: doing a thing for a laugh is doing it in jest, so for gives the first word; a laugh, a joke, is a jest

explanation.surface: Someone explains they only ate something as a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food into the body, i.e. to swallow or consume it.

clue.text: Tickled by 14 for one in the current era

indicators.note: the Muse sits in the era, so its letters go between the two letters of the era's abbreviation

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) labels years of the current era
the answer to 14-across, Terpsichore, is one of the nine Muses

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted by a modern-day dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tickled, in the sense of pleased or entertained, is being amused.

clue.text: Nice small top slips — being embraced by one naked causes awkwardness

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the altered French word is held inside the letters for one naked

parts.note: naked means nude

indicators.note: the top letter slips down a place within the French word

parts.note: in Nice, a French city, small is petit
the top letter of the word, its first

explanation.surface: A skimpy top slipping off someone who is half-dressed causes embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective meaning pleasant, but it is the French resort, so the word for small is French; its top letter slips down one place before it is embraced.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineptitude is a lack of skill or grace, which is clumsiness or awkwardness.

clue.text: Show anger in a different way: he's a gent, sincere at heart

indicators.note: the word for sincere sits at the heart of the rearranged letters
the letters are set out in another way, i.e. rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words are the material to be rearranged
sincere means honest

explanation.surface: An angry man's anger is shown differently because he is a sincere gentleman at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters split into two parts so the word for sincere can sit at their heart, straddling the answer's word breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: To grind one's teeth together is the classic display of fury or frustration.

clue.text: The late tragic Jesse Owens?

indicators.note: a tragic state is a wretched mess, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mournful reference to the deceased Olympic champion Jesse Owens.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesse Owens was an American sprinter who won four Olympic golds in 1936, an example of a track star; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Perhaps it's a pain having to eat trout's head for starters

indicators.note: the rearranged letters swallow the trout's head, holding it inside
perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: the letters of these words are rearranged

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of trout's

explanation.surface: A diner grumbles that eating trout's head as a first course is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges ITSAPAIN into ANIPASI, and 'having to eat' takes in T from 'trout's head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are Italian hors d'oeuvres served before the main meal, so appetisers or first courses.

clue.text: What's up with the Spanish setter's instruction?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: eh? is a way of asking what's that
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A puzzled solver asks what the crossword setter meant by an instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but here it is the dog breed, and the instruction is the command given to a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Heel is the command telling a dog such as a setter to walk close beside its owner.

clue.text: Start of exercise with 10, repeated thus on right muscle

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of exercise
10 is given twice: once as the Roman numeral X and again as the word TEN
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A fitness instruction: begin exercising with ten repetitions, as here, on the right muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads '10, repeated' as a rep count; in the wordplay it means 10 written twice, in numerals and in words.
explanation.definitionFit: An extensor is a muscle whose contraction straightens or extends a limb.

clue.text: In finale, Johnny at last became monetised

indicators.note: the singer's surname and the letter go inside the word for finale

parts.note: a finale is the end
Johnny Cash was the American country singer

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: last letter of became

explanation.surface: Johnny Cash finally cashed in at the end of his career.
explanation.definitionFit: To encash something is to convert it into money, which is what monetising means.

clue.text: Look to cover the centre of wound dressing

indicators.note: the word for look goes around the centre letter, covering it

parts.note: to look steadily is to gaze

indicators.note: picks out the middle letter of the five-letter word that follows

parts.note: middle letter of wound

explanation.surface: A nurse is told to examine a wound and bandage its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauze is a thin open-weave fabric used as a medical bandage for wounds.

clue.text: Real gold, 24 ct, I fancy

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the answer to 24-down is then

indicators.note: fancy as a verb here means rearrange imaginatively, signalling an anagram

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thinks that 24-carat gold is the genuine article.
explanation.walkthrough: '24 ct' looks like a carat rating, but 24 is a cross-reference to 24-down, and ct with I is the material for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something authentic is genuine, not fake: the real thing.

clue.text: Hapless fellow finally dines: terribly posh establishments with awful working conditions

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of each of the two words

parts.note: last letter of hapless
last letter of fellow
dines means eats

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: An unlucky man eats in places that are far too smart, yet the sentence ends with grim factories.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweatshops are factories where labourers toil long hours for low pay in poor and often unsafe conditions.

clue.text: See 4
Outlines school team playing pieces regularly

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moving about, rearranged
regularly takes every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: alternate letters of pieces

explanation.surface: A school team is playing pieces in a regular game, perhaps chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Schematics are diagrams showing the outline or plan of a system or circuit.

clue.text: Unorthodox priest with job providing inspiration to dance

indicators.note: unorthodox, departing from the usual form, signals that the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of priest are rearranged
a chore is a routine job

explanation.surface: A cleric who breaks with convention has a task that gets people dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Terpsichore is the Greek Muse of dance, so she is the one who inspires dancers.

clue.text: See 17
Sneering at origins of severe cases of rampant new flu variant

indicators.note: the origins of words are their first letters, one per word

parts.note: first letter of severe
first letter of cases
first letter of of
first letter of rampant
first letter of new

indicators.note: a variant is a changed form, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is dismissive about how severe cases arose from a widespread new flu strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Scornful of something means contemptuous of it, which is what sneering at it expresses.

clue.text: Way to test attractive and unusual scenario: men becoming mature!

parts.note: magnetic means attractive, drawing things to it

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these letters join the next word's in the anagram
these letters join the previous word's in the anagram
to mature is to age, here in its -ing form

explanation.surface: A strange scenario in which men grow up proves an attractive way to test something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges SCENARIOMEN into RESONANCEIM, and AGING joins its IM to make IMAGING.
explanation.definitionFit: An MRI scan is a medical diagnostic procedure, a method of examining the body's interior.

clue.text: Secret family decree in advance

parts.note: a clan is an extended family
to destine is to ordain or decide beforehand

explanation.surface: A family keeps a ruling, made ahead of time, hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Clandestine means done secretly or covertly, kept hidden from others.

clue.text: Occasionally in the present, as well as in the past

parts.note: now means at the present time
and means as well as
then means at that past time

explanation.surface: A statement that something holds in the present as it did in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Now and then is an idiom for from time to time, sometimes but not regularly.

clue.text: Lauder mascara's top value

parts.note: Estée Lauder is the cosmetics brand, named after its founder

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of mascara's

explanation.surface: The best-value mascara made by the cosmetics firm Estée Lauder.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem something is to prize it or hold it in high regard.

clue.text: Call round

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a circle or circular band

explanation.walkthrough: Two plain words that look like an instruction to telephone someone; each is a meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a phone call and a circular shape such as a band for the finger.

clue.text: One egg and one roast cooked for starters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a nit is the egg of a louse
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: cooked, in the sense of altered or fiddled, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe: an egg and a roast prepared as first courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' looks like the dinner-table sense, but it means people who start things off.
explanation.definitionFit: Initiators are those who begin or set something in motion, i.e. the ones who start things.

clue.text: See 4
See 19
Unlikely relief at chancellor's contribution

indicators.note: the answer is a contribution made by these words, a part of their letters

parts.note: the answer runs across these words

explanation.surface: Taxpayers feel relieved at what the Chancellor of the Exchequer, Britain's finance minister, has to offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat chance is an ironic idiom meaning there is very little likelihood of something.

clue.text: Grumpy pirate's not quiet

indicators.note: not means the word for quiet is excluded from the pirate

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered buccaneer is anything but silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means angry, cross or bad-tempered.

clue.text: Permission to take off uniform in misleading nice clue

indicators.note: take off means the letter for uniform is removed from the pool of letters
a misleading clue leads astray, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A setter is allowed to take off the uniform in a deceptive clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove U from NICECLUE and rearrange the remaining letters, as 'misleading' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence is official authorisation, a formal grant of permission to do something.

clue.text: Jews initially hate allowing skirts to be pulled back

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: first letter of hate
first letter of allowing

indicators.note: pulled back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: midis are mid-calf-length skirts

explanation.surface: Members of a strict faith dislike being allowed to pull back their skirts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hasidim are adherents of Hasidism, an ultra-Orthodox Jewish movement.
